Dates written out in reports, as ISO dates

Source: R/ovr.R
ovrdte.Rd

Finds the first date written in each text, in English or French, and gives it as YYYY-MM-DD, the form that sorts and that as.Date() reads. "January 5, 2023", "Jan. 5th 2023", "5 January 2023", "5th of January, 2023", "5 janvier 2023" and "2023-01-05" all give "2023-01-05".

Usage

ovrdte(x)

Arguments

x

The texts: a character vector.

Value

A character vector the length of x: the first date of each as YYYY-MM-DD, NA where there is none (or x is NA).

Details

Month names are English or French, whole or abbreviated (with or without a full stop), in any case, French accents optional; the day may carry an ordinal ("1st", "1er"). A day that does not exist ("February 30, 2023") is passed over, and the search goes on to the next date in the text. The reading never depends on the session's locale.

Examples

ovrdte(c("January 5, 2023", "le 1er février 2021", "no date"))
#> [1] "2023-01-05" "2021-02-01" NA          
ovrdte("On February 30, 2023 or rather March 2, 2023, the SIU ...")
#> [1] "2023-03-02"
as.Date(ovrdte("Date: April 28, 2023"))
#> [1] "2023-04-28"
